chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Jamil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When there is a group of people in a gathering, then (another) group proceeds and enters, it is upon the one entering last, when he enters, that he should greet them (with salam).

key_terms.الدَّاخِلُ أَخِيراً: The one who enters last — the latecomer who joins an existing gathering
key_terms.مَجْلِس: Gathering, sitting, assembly — a social setting where people meet
key_terms.يُسَلِّم: To give the salam greeting — the Islamic greeting of peace (السَّلَام عَلَيْكُمْ)

ai.seo_question: Who is obligated to initiate the greeting when joining an existing gathering according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that when someone joins a gathering that is already in session, the obligation of initiating the greeting (salam) falls upon the latecomer. This reflects the Islamic etiquette principle that the one who arrives later bears the social responsibility of acknowledging those already present, showing respect and courtesy to the established gathering.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Umar Bin Abdul Aziz, from Jameel, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When a group enters into a gathering, then (another) group proceeds and enters, so it is upon the ones entering later, when they do enter, that they should greet (السَّلَامُ) upon them (the first one)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz from Jamil from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
If two groups attend the same meeting, the group entering last should offer greetings of peace to those who have entered first.”
